ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (dark/black) distribution across the visible surface. High-intensity pixels (white) are limited to <5% of the total surface area, primarily localized as small circular clusters and transient water spray.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Homogeneous low-intensity contiguous region across both lobes. No macro-scale geometric white blobs or banding patterns. Sparse, high-contrast point-clusters are non-uniformly distributed across the dark field.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped central depression. Calculated internal angle of approximately 45-50 degrees with significant vertical depth relative to the horizontal fluke axis.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous, high-frequency irregular serration pattern. Pixel-amplitude of peaks varies between 3 to 12 pixels. The right lobe exhibits a more densely packed sequence of peaks compared to the left lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex trajectory sweeping laterally from the median notch toward the distal tips of the lobes.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Detection of multiple small, roughly circular high-contrast (white) pixel clusters distributed across the dark surface, notably on the medial sections and lower-left lobe quadrant.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Multiple localized circular white scars or lesions, likely barnacle attachment remnants, are visible against the dark ventral pigmentation.
other_distinctive_markers: Significant pixel occlusion in the lower central and left regions caused by transient high-intensity spray (water droplets) during fluke emergence.
